PullRequest.Title: Recommend connectors from prompt URLs

Fixes #341453
Companion product metadata: microsoft/vscode-distro#1469

The new-session composer stays quiet until its prompt contains a recognized connector URL. Matching connectors then appear through the existing chat tips UI, inheriting its setting, eligibility, layout, navigation, accessibility, and session visibility behavior.

## Implementation

- Reads connector display names, task descriptions, image URLs, and recognized URL associations from trusted product metadata through the `urls` field.
- Supports Linear, Notion, WorkIQ, Azure Data Explorer, Sentry, and Slack.
- Uses the standard chat tip surface instead of a separate recommendation row.
- Extends chat tips with an optional 16px decorative image. Connector icons use the 2px `--vscode-cornerRadius-xSmall` token; ordinary tips remain text-only.
- Shows no connector tip without a matching URL or when chat tips, the customization marketplace, Copilot connectors, or connector recommendations are disabled.
- Keeps the selected recommendation stable while its matching URL set is unchanged.
- Exposes every match through the existing Previous Tip and Next Tip controls when prompts contain URLs for multiple connectors.
- Ignores product names, email addresses, lookalike hosts, and connector domains embedded in another URL's path.
- Suppresses a dismissed connector for the composer session and follows the standard tip session-dismissal behavior.
- Opens the exact Copilot Connector detail by carrying both the stable product key and display name. Connector lookup supports opaque catalog names without falling back to an error notification.

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The call path is explicit: SharedChatInputComposer forwards each inputEditor.onDidChangeModelContent event through onDidChangeInput; the new listener calls update immediately; getInputValue reaches inputEditor.getValue; and the new matcher loops through input.length while allocating token slices/lowercase strings. The composer and restored/prefilled draft paths impose no text-length bound. Exact milliseconds depend on prompt size, so severity is medium rather than high.
Findings.PerformanceResource: UI-thread CPU plus temporary full-input/token strings, sets, and URL objects.
Findings.PerformanceScaling: Each edit costs O(L) in prompt length plus token allocations (and a small current connector-domain factor); appending N characters one by one is O(N^2) cumulative parsing, while K edits after pasting an L-character prompt cost O(K*L).
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: Increased input latency and potential dropped frames while editing long prompts, with additional GC pressure.
Findings.PreviousBehavior: Before the PR, connector recommendations were static cards initialized once; the component did not subscribe to prompt changes or read/tokenize the editor model on each edit.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: Every new-session editor content change now synchronously reads the full Monaco model and reparses the entire prompt for connector URLs before the input event returns.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: The added subscription at line 67 invokes update() synchronously for every composer input event; update() then calls findMatchingConnectorRecommendationIds(this.options.getInputValue(), ...) at line 117. That new helper walks the entire string, slices every whitespace-delimited token, lowercases it, and constructs URL objects for URL-like tokens.
Findings.Title: Avoid reparsing the entire prompt on every keystroke
Findings.Impact: After a user pastes or restores a long prompt and continues typing, each keystroke performs a full synchronous reparse on the renderer/UI thread, increasing key-to-paint latency and temporary-allocation/GC pressure; sufficiently large prompts can visibly hitch typing.
Findings.Evidence: SharedChatInputComposer fires onDidChangeInput directly from Monaco's onDidChangeModelContent and getInputValue() returns ChatWidget.getInput(), which calls inputEditor.getValue(). The newly added matcher iterates from 0 through input.length on every call, slices each token, lowercases it, and may instantiate URL for each URL-like token; no debounce, scheduler, length cap, or incremental cache exists. Even when the connector match set is unchanged, update() completes this scan and constructs a candidate tip before its tipStateKey early return.
Findings.Recommendation: Keep URL recommendation work off the immediate content-change path: coalesce/debounce to the latest prompt and update an incremental token/hostname cache from Monaco change ranges (or otherwise bound the scanned text). Also create the Markdown tip only after the matched ID set actually changes.

Scenarios.Scenario: Typing or editing a new-session prompt after pasting/restoring substantial text
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Monaco onDidChangeModelContent synchronously fires SharedChatInputComposer.onDidChangeInput, whose new listener calls update(), inputEditor.getValue(), and the full URL matcher before the edit handler returns.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Full prompt length and whitespace-delimited token count on every edit; current connector/domain metadata is small (the described rollout has six connectors), so prompt length is the dominant factor.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Single-threaded and serialized on the renderer/UI event path; rapid edits are not debounced or coalesced, so every delivered model-change event performs a scan.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: There is no scan-result cache or coalescing; each editor change rereads and reparses the latest full prompt. Connector metadata is held in maps, but token/hostname results are discarded after every event.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the synchronous event-to-full-scan call path and per-token allocations are explicit in the code.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Normal short prompts make the scan cheap; the exact prompt length and device speed needed for visible jank are unmeasured. Restored drafts, command-prefilled prompts, and direct editor input are not length-bounded, so long prompts are realistically reachable.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reportable medium-severity repeated-work regression: the diff adds an unbounded O(prompt length) synchronous parse and allocations to every input event, whereas the prior recommendation UI did no per-edit work.

Scenarios.Scenario: Opening a new-session composer with an empty prompt
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Widget construction parses product icon URIs, registers the provider/listeners, and runs one empty-input update. No connector network/catalog operation blocks construction.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Load the optional connector icon assigned to an img element.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Zero image requests at default empty-prompt startup; later, at most one currently selected connector icon is attached to the rendered tip.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The old recommendation component rendered every configured connector card and assigned every icon during startup, causing all card images to load eagerly.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: No image network request blocks initial composer construction; browser loading is asynchronous when a tip appears.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Configured connector count, currently a small product-owned set.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: One synchronous initialization; no fan-out. Image loading is deferred because no tip exists without a matching URL.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: With an empty prompt, matching returns empty. Product metadata is copied into maps once. No connector icon is requested until a matching tip is rendered; browser image caching governs subsequent renders.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the constructor no longer creates card DOM or icon renderers and the tip is undefined for empty input.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The old configured recommendation count and browser cache warmth vary, but the changed startup path clearly does no more boundary work and generally less.
Scenarios.Verdict: No regression; the diff removes eager card/icon rendering and avoids startup image requests.

Scenarios.Scenario: Showing and navigating connector tips for one or multiple matching URLs
Scenarios.CriticalPath: When a URL first starts or stops matching, the provider fires onDidChangeTip and presenters synchronously clear/rebuild the small tip DOM. Image decode/network completion is asynchronous.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Set an img src for the selected tip icon.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One icon URL for the selected matching connector; navigation may expose one additional icon per user action, subject to browser cache.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: All recommendation-card icons were assigned and loaded eagerly when the widget initialized, rather than one lazily selected icon.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The text tip renders without awaiting the image request; the request is off the synchronous input critical path, though DOM replacement occurs synchronously on a match transition.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of distinct matched connectors navigated by the user, not the number of prompt tokens after the match set stabilizes.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: One selected tip is rendered at a time. Navigation is user-serialized; there is no burst across all matching connectors.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: A cold icon may require one browser request; warm navigation normally reuses the browser cache. Match state is kept stable while the hostname set is unchanged.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: only the active IChatTip carries one icon and tip changes are gated by tipStateKey.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Remote icon cache headers and navigation frequency are unknown; the changed cardinality is lower than the old eager behavior.
Scenarios.Verdict: No separate performance finding; tip DOM rerendering occurs only when selected/matched IDs change, and icon boundary cardinality is reduced from eager-all to one-at-a-time.

Scenarios.Scenario: Activating a connector recommendation to open its marketplace detail
Scenarios.CriticalPath: After explicit link activation, opening the customization editor and getConnectors() must complete before connector detail can be shown. This is user-triggered, not on typing/startup.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Retrieve the Copilot connector catalog via CopilotConnectorsService.getConnectors().
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One catalog service call per explicit open; warm calls are served from the 60-second cache, cold/stale calls issue one catalog query.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Clicking an old connector card called the same marketplace command and showCopilotConnectorDetail(), which already awaited one getConnectors() call.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The connector detail waits for this call, exactly as before.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: At most 1000 cached connector objects for the fallback local scan, once per explicit open.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: One command and one catalog retrieval for a normal click. The reviewed diff does not add a per-connector loop of boundary calls or alter service concurrency.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: CopilotConnectorsService returns its in-memory connector list for 60 seconds after refresh; a cold/stale catalog invokes refresh. The new display-name fallback is a second in-memory linear find only after the same catalog result arrives.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the changed method adds only an optional second local Array.find by displayName after the unchanged getConnectors call.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Cold request latency and catalog size vary; the service caps connectors at 1000 and caches successful refreshes for 60 seconds.
Scenarios.Verdict: No regression; no new boundary or fan-out is introduced, and the additional fallback scan is bounded, user-triggered, and negligible relative to the existing catalog retrieval.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over all 21 changed files. Submitted one finding for synchronous full-prompt rescanning on every editor change. Startup rendering, tip image loading, navigation, and connector-detail catalog access were traced and did not introduce additional reportable regressions.

Stats.CostNote: Copilot SDK reports nano-AI units and model billing multipliers; it does not provide a USD conversion.
